title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 2nd version, 18-20 June 1986). Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'tame' (modérée) geometry combinatorially. The data are a set M of 'multiplicative' elementary pieces (cells or simplices) ordered by ≤ (inclusion), and a set 𝓕 of 'figures'. Each figure F is identified with the subset F~ = {X ∈ M | X ≤ F} via 𝓕 → 𝔓(M). The previous page encoded the 'moral' content of (M, 𝓕) as the order ≤ plus a symmetric reflexive disjunction-type relation ≬ satisfying (1.36). This page begins the treatment of the refinement relation ≪. The next page makes its intended meaning explicit: 'G is a sub-figure of a subdivision of F'.

(*) The shadow (ombre) Omb(F) = {X ∈ M | X ≪ F} is the set of all elementary pieces occurring in subdivisions of F, a combinatorial stand-in for the point set of F.

(**) The multishadow Multiomb(F) = {Omb(X) | X ∈ F~} is the family of shadows of the cells of F. Grothendieck wants it to be a 'figure ensembliste' (a stratified set) in M, faithfully indexed by F~. Its strata are the Omb(X)°, which on the natural reading are the cells whose 'carrier' is exactly X, analogous to open simplices. The order ≤ on F~ should correspond to inclusion (of closures of strata).

Dependence on ≪_𝓕 versus ≪_M. Definition (*) a priori uses ≪ between M and 𝓕, but he claims it reduces to ≪ inside M. Two axioms secure this.
- C4: X ≪ Y in M implies X ≤ Y.
- C5 (1.37): if X ≪ F, the set F^X = {Y ∈ M | X ≪ Y ≤ F} (the cells of F 'verified' by X) has a smallest element. This is the carrier, i.e. the smallest face of F whose subdivision contains X, as in simplicial approximation.
- Corollary: X ≪ F holds iff there is Y ∈ M with X ≪ Y ≤ F. Hence ≪_𝓕 is the composite of ≪_M with ≤, and Omb(F) = ∪_{Y∈F~} Omb(Y).

A crossed-out C6 attempted an existence or minimality axiom (some Y ≪ X with additional properties, 'cf C4') and was abandoned.

Final NB: in Multiomb(X) the strata Omb(X)° are nonempty, trivially, since X ∈ Omb(X)°.

Next page: X is recovered as the ≪-largest element of Omb(X). So F ↦ Multiomb(F) is injective, and G ≤ F iff Multiomb(G) ≤ Multiomb(F). On 19 June Grothendieck abandons this geometric meaning of ≪ as unnatural even in the simplicial case. Purpose overall: a point-free, combinatorial reconstruction of tame topology, recovering figures as stratified sets from a poset of cells with a refinement relation.
errors: The NB 'X ∈ Omb(X)°' presupposes reflexivity X ≪ X (subdivision includes the trivial one), which is not stated as an axiom on this page.
Nonemptiness of the 'open' stratum also needs that X does not lie in Omb(X') for X' < X. This follows from C4 plus antisymmetry of ≤, but the definition of Omb(X)° is not written here.
Grothendieck at first leaves it unclear whether (*) needs ≪ on 𝓕; the claim that it depends only on ≪_M is justified only after C4/C5 and the Corollary.
C6 is crossed out unfinished; the axiom system is incomplete on this page, and the whole viewpoint is abandoned on 19 June (next page).

ideas.what: Shadow Omb(F): set of elementary cells refining a figure, as a point-free substitute for its underlying set
ideas.modern_name: Set of cells of all subdivisions; point-free/combinatorial model of a polyhedron (cf. locale-theoretic or cellular models)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Combinatorial topology tradition (subdivision posets); o-minimal triangulation (van den Dries, Shiota) for the tame setting
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of 'topologie modérée' appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (1984)

ideas.what: Multishadow Multiomb(F): stratification of Omb(F) indexed faithfully by the cells of F, strata = cells with given carrier
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of a regular cell complex into open cells; face poset as stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (regular CW complexes, face posets; Björner for face posets)

ideas.what: Axiom C5: existence of a smallest cell Y of F with X ≪ Y ≤ F
ideas.modern_name: Carrier (support) of a cell of a subdivision; minimal carrier as in simplicial approximation

ideas.what: Corollary: ≪ between cell and figure factors as ≪ in M composed with ≤
ideas.modern_name: Relational composition / reduction of a relation on figures to a relation on cells

ideas.what: Injectivity of F ↦ Multiomb(F) and order-compatibility (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Faithful embedding of figures into stratified sets of a poset

missed.claim: An attempted axiomatic, point-free foundation of tame topology from a poset of cells with an order ≤, a disjunction relation ≬ and a refinement relation ≪. Figures are recovered as stratified sets ('multiombres') whose strata are carriers. The thread is abandoned the next day, and C6 is left crossed out.
missed.quote: Je veux que cette multiombre soit une figure ensembliste dans M, ... indexée fidèlement par F~
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: There is no standard axiomatic 'cell-poset' foundation of o-minimal or tame topology that avoids points. This is a documented early attempt, of interest for historians of the Esquisse's 'topologie modérée' programme and possibly for synthetic or combinatorial approaches to tame geometry. Mathematically it is mostly elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Unpublished, fairly elementary axiomatics (shadows, carriers, stratification by carrier) in Grothendieck's tame-topology project. It is historically interesting as a concrete trace of the Esquisse programme, but self-abandoned the next day and close to classical combinatorial topology.
transcription_corrections: '{+et indépendante par F~+}' should read approximately '{+et indexée fidèlement par F~+}'.
'il est clair que la multiombre ne dépend {+que+} de ≪_M (non de ≪_𝓕)': the parenthesis reads closer to '(au lieu de ≪_𝓕)'.
The first sentence begins 'En principe (*) utilise la connaissance de ≪ dans 𝓕 dans sa notation, mais il résulte des axiomes qu'elle ne dépend que de ≪'.
Margin for the Cor reads as an iff: 'si X∈M, F∈𝓕, pour que X ≪ F il faut et il suffit qu'il existe Y ∈ M avec X ≪ Y ≤ F'.
Margin 'Ainsi X≪F dans 𝓕 ...' likely reads 'Ainsi X ≪ F dans 𝓕 équivaut à X ≪ Y, Y ≤ F, Y ∈ M (≪ dans M)'.
Margin near the stratification reads approximately 'avec la relation d'ordre ≤ dans F~ correspondant à l'inclusion des [adhérences des strates de] Multiomb(F)'.
Bottom NB reads 'dans Multiomb(X), les Omb(X)° ≠ ∅, est trivial, car X ∈ Omb(X)°'.
The struck C6 includes 'b) Y ≪ X' ≤ X ⇒ X' = X' and refers '(cf C4)'.
The first-page text 'C4 Si X,Y ∈ M tels que X≪Y alors X ≤ Y' is in the left margin, not the main text.
